title: Book 7 — Polymnia, Chapter 106
paragraphs: Mascames, whom he left behind here, proved to be a man of such qualities that to him alone Xerxes used to send gifts, reckoning him the best of all the men whom he or Darius had appointed as governors. He used to send him gifts every year, and so did Artaxerxes son of Xerxes afterwards to Mascames's descendants. For even before this campaign, governors had been appointed throughout Thrace and everywhere around the Hellespont; but all of these — both in Thrace and on the Hellespont — were conquered by the Greeks after this expedition, except only the one at Doriscus. Many tried to take Mascames at Doriscus, but none ever succeeded. For this reason the gifts are sent continually for him from whatever Persian king reigns at the time.
